read.thesis: A bank, not a capital-cycle story: 1H26 PBT up 23% to $19.5bn with RoTE 18.2%, but ~$2.2bn of the rise is notable items and CET1 fell to 14.1%.

triggers.label: Banking NII raised to at least $46bn
triggers.quote: We now expect banking NII of at least $46bn in 2026, reflecting a continued favourable interest rate outlook

triggers.label: Buy-back up to $1bn restarted
triggers.quote: We also resumed share buy-backs (up to $1bn), three quarters after we paused them

triggers.label: NIM 1.61%, up 4bps
triggers.quote: Net interest margin (‘NIM’) of 1.61% was 4 basis points (‘bps‘) higher compared with 1H25

triggers.label: CET1 14.9% → 14.1%
triggers.quote: Common equity tier 1 (‘CET1’) capital ratio of 14.1% decreased by 0.8 percentage points

guidance.quote: We now expect banking NII of at least $46bn in 2026
including a return on average tangible equity (‘RoTE’) of 17% or better for 2026, 2027 and 2028

guidance.metric: ECL charge as % of average gross loans 2026
guidance.quote: We continue to expect an ECL charge as a percentage of average gross customer loans to be around 45bps
The Group remains on track to deliver year-on-year growth in operating expenses of approximately 1% in 2026 on a target basis.
We intend to continue to manage the CET1 capital ratio within our medium-term target range of 14% to 14.5%.

prior_guidance_check.quote: We had previously provided banking NII guidance of around $46bn for 2026.
We remain confident in achieving the targets we set out in February 2026

red_flags.label: Notable items flatter PBT growth
red_flags.quote: The increase primarily reflected a year-on-year net favourable impact of $2.2bn from notable items.

red_flags.label: CET1 down 0.8pp
red_flags.quote: reflecting the impact of the privatisation of Hang Seng Bank Limited

red_flags.label: Herald litigation exposure
red_flags.quote: the eventual financial impact could be significantly different
